sources.title: Spanish Ministry of Culture: Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba
sources.note: Definition directly available through indexed original result; direct open returned 429. Gives 929 to 1031, proclamation and religious/political title.

sources.title: Ceuta Cultural Heritage: Medina Sabta
sources.note: Full indexed original section Bastión del califato cordobés en el norte de África (931 to 1009): local alliances, occupation 24 March 931, 958 reversal, 996 to 998 conflict, 1009 revolt and taifa fragmentation. Direct open exceeded size limit.

sources.title: NYU ISAW and Andalusian museums: Building a Capital
sources.note: Direct full exhibition essay. Use urban organization, Salón Rico and Ja’far. Do not infer absence of women/children from archaeology or repeat etymology of ataurique.

sources.title: NYU ISAW: Influences and Rivalries
sources.note: Direct full essay; Islamic Coins from al-Andalus subsection. Also explains competing Umayyad, Abbasid and Fatimid claims.

sources.title: Madinat al-Zahra archaeological ensemble: Eastern Service Quarters
sources.note: Indexed original found via exact title and horno construido. Full Spanish and English text on museum asset 498848380; direct canonical URL errored. Clay oven, kitchen official proposed, private and double latrines. Sex of workers is an interpretation and omitted.

sources.title: Madinat al-Zahra archaeological ensemble: Court of the Pillars
sources.note: Indexed full original description. Two latrines, sarcophagus basin, hypothetical 950 to 960 construction, exact function unknown.

sources.title: NYU ISAW: Dining with the Caliph
sources.note: Direct full essay. Restrict to excavated tenth-century tableware and stove. Thirteenth-century cookbook and implausibly universal single-use unglazed pottery claim are deliberately excluded.

sources.title: NYU ISAW: Knowledge as Power
sources.note: Direct full essay, learning/library, Keeping Time, Kitab al-Tasrif subsections. Displayed medical manuscript is dated 1464, not the author’s autograph. Doha astrolabe made in Iran, so not used as local find.

sources.title: Louvre OA 4068: Pyxis bearing the name of al-Mughira
sources.note: Direct catalogue Description/Inscriptions, Ernst Kühnel reading 1971: بركة من الله; French translation Bénédiction de Dieu. Around lower edge of lid; Arabic Kufic; date AH 357 / 967 to 968; object dated 968. No visual autopsy claimed.

sources.title: Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba: Maqsura restoration project
sources.note: Indexed full official project text, first paragraph: octagonal mihrab chamber, shell dome, horseshoe entrance and Byzantine mosaic makers.

sources.title: NYU ISAW: The Rise and Fall of an Islamic Capital
sources.note: Direct full essay. Child Hisham, al-Mansur, sieges, later reuse and 1911 excavations. Page has anomalous 928 proclamation; use Ministry’s 929 instead.

sources.title: UNESCO: Caliphate City of Medina Azahara
sources.note: Direct indexed official statement, Integrity and description: preserved infrastructure and everyday objects, excavation extent. Its compressed 1009 to 1010 ending wording is not used for formal 1031 abolition.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Umayyad caliphate ruled from Córdoba between 929 and 1031, sponsoring monumental buildings, scholarship and skilled crafts.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Independent card, not an emirate alias. Imported 1000 to 1100 historical-basemaps polygon covers Iberia and broad North Africa (bbox saved in identity.json). Historical caliphate 929 to 1031. Public overview and ending flag date mismatch; overview and Ceuta paragraph flag nonuniform African control. No geometry repair attempted. Existing emirate URLs deliberately not reused, preventing prior-source budget collision.
